swot_scope: Acme Compliance entering the German mid-market (200-2,000 staff) in 2027

strengths.text: Automated GDPR record-of-processing export already used by 140 EU customers
strengths.evidence: Product analytics: 140 accounts ran the export in Q1 2026

strengths.text: Median onboarding of 9 days versus 35 for the two incumbent vendors
strengths.evidence: Implementation logs for 60 onboardings in 2025; incumbent figures from public reviews

strengths.text: Two in-house data-protection lawyers who write the product's policy templates
strengths.evidence: Templates cited as the deciding factor in 3 lost-deal reversals

weaknesses.text: No German-language UI or support team
weaknesses.evidence: Support staffed in English only; 4 German trials churned citing language

weaknesses.text: No ISO 27001 certificate, which German procurement asks for by default
weaknesses.evidence: Requested in 7 of 9 German RFPs in 2025

weaknesses.text: Sales cycle with regulated buyers averages 5 months
weaknesses.evidence: CRM, 2025 closed-won deals in EU finance

opportunities.text: NIS2 transposition makes supplier security reviews mandatory for mid-sized German firms
opportunities.evidence: National NIS2 implementation law and regulator guidance

opportunities.text: The main incumbent raised mid-market prices 30% in 2026
opportunities.evidence: Published price list and 3 prospect emails

threats.text: A German-first local vendor is bundling with a large payroll provider
threats.mitigation: Partner with a works-council tooling vendor before launch

threats.text: Data-residency demands could require a German hosting region we do not run yet
threats.mitigation: Price a Frankfurt region before committing to a launch date

tows_actions.action: Lead with NIS2 supplier-review automation built on the existing export
Get ISO 27001 before the NIS2 deadline wave
Use the 9-day onboarding as the proof point against the bundled local vendor
Do not launch until German support is staffed; a delay costs less than churn
